chunks: With this chain of transmission, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbdillāh ibn Zurārah, from Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Hishām ibn Sālim, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: concerning
A man approaching a woman in what is other than the private part while she is menstruating—he said: “There is no harm, if he avoids that place.”

key_terms.الرَّجُلِ: the man addressed in the legal ruling
key_terms.الْفَرْجِ: the private part, whose use is being specifically prohibited here
key_terms.الْمَرْأَةَ: the woman involved in the ruling
key_terms.الْمَوْضِعَ: the particular place meant in the ruling
key_terms.حَائِضٌ: a woman in the state of menstruation
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm or objection in the ruling

ai.seo_question: Is intimacy with one’s wife allowed during menstruation if intercourse is avoided?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding intimacy with a menstruating woman. It states that there is no objection to intimacy short of intercourse, so long as the specific prohibited place is avoided.
